critical_qualifiers: Conclusion The Secret to Results That Last THERE IS AN ancient Greek parable known as the Sorites Paradox,fn1 which talks about the effect one small action can have when repeated enough times
One formulation of the paradox goes as follows: Can one coin make a person rich?
But what if you add another?
At some point, you will have to admit that no one can be rich unless one coin can make him or her so
We can say the same about atomic habits
Can one tiny change transform your life?
But what if you made another?
The holy grail of habit change is not a single 1 percent improvement, but a thousand of them
In the beginning, small improvements can often seem meaningless because they get washed away by the weight of the system

Each of the people, teams, and companies we have covered has faced different circumstances, but ultimately progressed in the same way: through a commitment to tiny, sustainable, unrelenting improvements
